newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia starts bankruptcy case against tax laggards.
newsitem.headline: Russia starts bankruptcy case against tax laggards.

text.p: The Russian government has started bankruptcy suits against four companies that owe large sums in back taxes and warned seven others to pay taxes within a week, a senior government official said on Monday.
The government will also examine 12 other companies which it believes are in arrears, including several major oil producers, said Federal Department for Bankruptcy head Pyotr Mostovoi.
Earlier this month the government wrote to six companies saying they faced bankruptcy proceedings if they did not pay their tax bills, he told a news conference.
The government has now forwarded documents in two of these cases to the courts, and is preparing documents in the other two cases, he said.

The four companies are carmaker AO Moskvich, heavy truckmaker AO KamAZ, the Krasnodarnefteorgsintez oil refinery which belongs to oil group Rosneft, and the AO Achinsky Glinozemny Kombinat alumina company.

Tax arrears since the beginning of this year for the four companies are as follows -- Moskvich 271 billion roubles, KamAZ 85 billion, Krasnodarnefteorgsintez 93 billion and Achinsky Glinozemny 88 billion.
"You can work on the assumption that we have started bankruptcy cases against all four companies," Mostovoi said.
He said the companies could provide the government with papers proving they did not owe taxes.
Two of the original six -- Tatneft and Purneftegaz -- had done so but only after they had been threatened with bankruptcy, he said.
The Russian government has started a major crackdown against tax dodgers in an effort to improve tax revenues, which have so far run at only 74 percent of budgeted levels.
The International Monetary Fund, worried about the tax shortfall, last week delayed payment of the next tranche of its $10 billion loan to Russia.
Mostovoi said that the government had sent letters to a further seven minor companies, which had paid less than 20 percent of this year's taxes.
Mostovoi said the government planned to examine a further 12 companies behind in paying taxes.

These include oil group NK Sidanko's production unit AO Varyoganneftegaz, Sibneft's main production unit AO Noyabrsknefegaz, and Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya's AO Nizhnevartovskneftegaz production unit and troubled carmaker AO ZiL.
